findings.title: Team admin permission check uses AND instead of OR, excluding team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles while `isTeamOwner` only returns true for OWNER, the AND combination collapses to 'owner only'. As a result, team members with the ADMIN role (but not OWNER) are denied permission to add guests even though the variable name and intended UX (editBookingActions menu item shown to all users regardless of exact role) imply admins should be allowed. This should be `||` (or just use `isTeamAdmin` alone), otherwise legitimate team admins will get a FORBIDDEN error when trying to use this feature.

findings.title: EventManager is built with the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` use `ctx.user` (the person triggering the mutation), not the booking's organizer (`booking.user`). The handler explicitly allows team admins/owners and attendees (not just the organizer) to add guests, so in those cases the EventManager will be instantiated with the wrong account's calendar/video credentials. This can cause `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` to silently fail, update the wrong calendar, or throw, because the acting user may have no credentials at all or different ones than the organizer who actually owns the calendar event.

findings.title: Blacklisted guest email filter is bypassed by case variation
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are compared against it without being lower-cased (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). An attacker/user can bypass the blacklist simply by submitting the email with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` instead of `blocked@example.com`), defeating the purpose of `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`.

findings.title: Duplicate-attendee check is case sensitive, allowing duplicate attendees with different email casing
findings.body: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` performs an exact, case-sensitive string comparison. If an existing attendee's email is stored as `Jane@Example.com` and a new guest is submitted as `jane@example.com`, the guest will not be recognized as a duplicate and a second attendee record with the 'same' email (different case) will be created, leading to duplicate emails sent and inconsistent attendee lists.

findings.title: Email send failure is silently swallowed with no error detail logged
findings.body: The catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, discarding the actual `err` object and using `console.log` instead of the project's structured logger (`@calcom/lib/logger`) used elsewhere. This makes it impossible to diagnose production email failures (e.g. SMTP errors, template rendering errors) from logs, and the handler still returns a success message to the client even though guest notification emails may not have been sent.

findings.title: Fallback error toast message is unreachable dead code
findings.body: `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` where `message` is built as a template literal `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` ``. A template literal always produces a non-empty string (even `"undefined: ..."` if `err.data?.code` is undefined), so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never execute. This also means users will see a raw, unlocalized error such as `undefined: emails_must_be_unique_valid` or `BAD_REQUEST: booking_not_found` instead of a friendly translated message in edge cases where `err.message` is not a recognized i18n key.

findings.title: Unsafe array access on calEvent.attendees[0] can throw if attendees list is empty
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` assumes `calEvent.attendees` always has at least one element. If this email class is ever invoked for an event with zero attendees (e.g. due to a filtering bug upstream or future reuse of this class), this will throw a runtime TypeError instead of degrading gracefully, breaking the whole email send flow (including the `Promise.all` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`).

findings.title: No automated tests added for the new add-guests feature
findings.body: This PR introduces a new tRPC handler/schema, a new dialog component, a new MultiEmail form component, and two new email templates, but no unit or integration tests were added (no tests for addGuests.handler.ts permission logic, duplicate/blacklist filtering, AddGuestsDialog validation, or MultiEmail behavior). Given the permission-check bug and case-sensitivity issues identified above, test coverage would have caught these regressions before merge.
